en: When water freezes into solid ice, it expands in volume by approximately nine percent, making ice less dense than liquid water.
Sound travels at 343 meters per second through air, but moves much faster at 5,960 meters per second through solid steel.
One liter of seawater contains 35 grams of dissolved salt, which is 70 times more salt than typical tap water.
Liquid nitrogen boils at negative 196 degrees Celsius, which is 196 degrees colder than the freezing point of pure water.
One gram of gold can be hammered into a one-square-meter sheet, making it far thinner than a single human hair.
When liquid water boils into a gas, one milliliter of water rapidly expands to fill about 1,700 milliliters of steam.
In a true solution like saltwater, dissolved particles are smaller than one nanometer, unlike larger particles found in heterogeneous suspensions.
Pure water has a neutral pH of exactly seven, while acidic lemon juice has a much lower pH of about two.
Osmium is the densest natural solid element, weighing 22.59 grams per cubic centimeter, which is roughly twice as dense as lead.
Absolute zero is negative 273.15 degrees Celsius, representing the lowest possible temperature where all atomic motion in matter theoretically stops.
Solid spider silk is a natural protein material that is five times stronger than steel of the exact same thickness.
Air is a mixture of 78 percent nitrogen and 21 percent oxygen, meaning it contains nearly four times more nitrogen than oxygen.
